desc: The Kandla-Bhatinda Oil Pipeline is a petroleum pipeline system in India that transports crude oil and refined petroleum products across Gujarat, Haryana, and Punjab. Commissioned in 1996, it has a total length of approximately 1,443 km. Its initial annual throughput capacity was 6 million metric tonnes per annum , later upgraded to 8.8 MMTPA.
